These petitions coming on for orders this day, the Court  the following :-
 ORDER
Since all these petitions involved commonality of facts and the point of law raised, all these petitions are taken up together and are be- ing decided by this common order.
2. For the sake of convenience, facts are taken from W.P.No.5660 of 2019.
3. The grievance of the petitioners in the instant cases is that their lands were taken away for the irrigation project namely Sanjali Mad- hyam Pariyojana Jalashay in District Sagar.

It is the case of the peti- tioner that though an award of acquisition of land has been passed in the matter of acquisition of land of the petitioners but no specific award in the matter of rehabilitation and resettlement benefits in terms of Section 31(1) of the right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Ac- quisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement, Act 2013 (hereinafter re- ferred to as 'Act of 2013').
4. The petitioner has placed reliance on the order passed by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.8332 of 2019.
5.

The reply filed by the State indicates that the matter for grant of rehabilitation and resettlement benefits in terms of Schedule-II to the Act of 2013 was considered and some proceedings of such consideration have been filed along with the reply.
However, it appears from perusal of the said documents, no award in the matter of benefit in terms of sec- ond Schedule to the Act of 2013 has been passed in the matter.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners has also argued that the second Schedule to the Act of 2013 provides for a number of benefits like pro- vision of housing units, land, employment and subsistence grant and other various rights which are provided in Serial No. 1 to 11 of second Schedule to the Act of 2013.

It is argued that the authority has not taken into consideration all of Ajit Kumar Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164774170/
6 such benefits as per entitlements of the petition- ers.

entities.text: Ajit Kumar Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.8332 of 2019 has held as under :-
"However, the petitioner has also claimed a relief that the benefit as required under Schedule-II of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisi- tion, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (here- inafter referred to as the 'Act,
2013') has not been provided to him despite the fact that his land has been acquired.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisi- tion, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the reply submitted by the respondents, they have stated that the petitioner is not entitled for such benefit as has been provided under Schedule-II of the Act, 2013 but in view of the judgment passed by the Coordinate Bench disposing of the petition, I am also inclined to dispose of the petition directing the petitioner to raise his dispute with regard to benefit mentioned in the Schedule-II of the Act, 2013 for which he is otherwise entitled.

The Collector shall consider the same and pass an appropriate order assigning reason as to whether the benefit under the existing circum- stances when land of the petitioner has been acquired can be granted to him or not because in Schedule-II appended with Sections 31(1), 38(1) and 105(3) of the Act, 2013 em- powers the Collector to take appropriate action, if so re- quired, but no order in this regard has been passed by the Collector in the present case.

Therefore, this petition is dis- posed of directing the petitioner to make a proper applica- tion/representation before the Collector asking relief as per Schedule-II of the Act, 2013 and if any application/repre- sentation is filed before the Collector

, he shall consider the same within a period of three months from the date of sub- mitting the same and pass a reasoned order ascribing as why benefit cannot be granted to the petitioner or if he is otherwise entitled to get the said benefit, the same be ex- tended to the petitioner."
8.
The above case was concerning the same project by which the pe- titioners have been affected.

In view of the aforesaid factual situation of the case and maintaining parity with the order passed in W.P.No.8332 of 2019, these petitions are also disposed of by directing the petitioners to file an appropriate application/representation before the Collector asking relief as per second Schedule of the Act of 2013 and if such application is filed before the Collector within a period of one month from today, then the Collector shall consider the same within a period of three months from the date of submitting the said application/representation and pass a reasoned order in terms of Section 31(1) of the Act of 2013.
9.
With the aforesaid direction, these petitions stand disposed of.

(VIVEK JAIN) JUDGE manju Ajit Kumar Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164774170/
